audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer repeatedly gives Galio 'Wind Wall' — an ability he does not have. It appears in whys[0], spikes[0].text, early, wants.you[0] and wants.foe[0], with advice built on 'baiting the wall'.
audit.why: Galio's W is Shield of Durand: a charged stance that damages and TAUNTS nearby enemies at 275 range on release, with a shield flag. Wind Wall belongs to Yasuo. Every sentence telling you to bait a projectile wall is coaching a mechanic that does not exist, and it hides the real threat, which is the taunt.
audit.corrected: Shield of Durand charges, then taunts inside 275 — stay outside it. Justice Punch is his 650-range dash knockup and Miasma grounds it.

audit.why: EVEN 5.5/10 is defensible for the lane itself: he has no ranged damage pattern that beats yours. The 47.24% comes from map play (Hero's Entrance, 4000-5500 range) rather than the lane.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[1..4] and phases[6] read 'Skill' while content win[N] and the packet read Cassiopeia for those rows.
audit.why: Cross-layer disagreement; the whys under those rows already describe you winning them.
audit.corrected: Those five sides -> Cassiopeia. Row 0 already agrees ('Skill' on both layers) and is untouched.

audit.why: Justice Punch 11/10/9/8/7, Shield of Durand 18/17/16/15/14, Winds of War 11/10/9/8/7, Hero's Entrance 180/160/140.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was tradeGood verbatim and dontsFull[2].d was tradeBad verbatim (lint COPY_PASTE_BLEED); dontsFull[0].d and dontsFull[1].d did not answer their titles.
audit.corrected: Rewritten against Justice Punch's grounding, Colossal Smash's splash and the R's facing rule.

edits.before: W changes the geometry: miasma GROUNDS dashes. Drop it on his engage path and the lane's mobility advantage evaporates.
edits.after: W changes the geometry: Miasma GROUNDS dashes. Drop it on the Justice Punch wind-up and the knockup never reaches you.

edits.before: - Galio Justice Punch: matchup-defining — His dash knockup — he has no engage while it is down. Check it before every step-up. - R Petrifying Gaze is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Justice Punch: 11s at rank 1, 7s maxed — the dash knockup, and Miasma grounds it. - Shield of Durand taunts every 18s at rank 1: never be inside 275 when it releases. - Hero's Entrance is 180s at rank 1.

edits.before: Q the last-hit window, E-E-E while the poison ticks, and walk back as it fades — three fangs and out, repeat until Galio is executable.
edits.after: Miasma grounds Justice Punch — drop the cloud on his 650-range wind-up and the knockup he lined up simply never arrives.

edits.before: Galio whiffs Justice Punch and the lane briefly belongs to you.
edits.after: Petrifying Gaze stuns only enemies facing you — meet the punch.

edits.before: That is Galio’s rehearsed moment — don’t audition for it.
edits.after: Miasma is your one answer to Justice Punch's knockup.

edits.before: Your miasma is the anti-dive — spending it on poke means the next engage arrives ungrounded and you have no boots to run.
edits.after: Colossal Smash splashes the whole wave and Winds of War ticks on top — inside his minions you take three sources at once.

edits.before: Spamming unpoisoned fangs at full mana cost, or holding W so long the dash you were saving it for already happened.
edits.after: A Justice Punch feint costs him 11 seconds and your Petrifying Gaze costs 120 — never trade those two on his terms.

edits.before: Galio wins by landing Justice Punch, denying your pattern, and front-loading the violence while your kit is still stretching.
edits.after: Galio wins by taunting you with Shield of Durand, knocking you up with Justice Punch, and landing Hero's Entrance on top.

edits.before: Carry by DPS — no mid matches your damage-per-second from two items; your job is staying alive long enough to prove it.
edits.after: Carry by range: his damage is Winds of War chip, so stay outside 275 taunt range and fang him for the whole 18 seconds.

edits.before: Wind Wall gives Galio a one-time answer but no real damage to punish your poke, keeping this close but skill-dependent
edits.after: Shield of Durand blunts your poke while charged, but he cannot punish back at range — close, and skill-dependent

edits.before: Galio's Wind Wall can block one Noxious Blast or Twin Fang, but he has no reliable way to threaten damage back, so your poke wins the exchange.
edits.after: Shield of Durand blunts the poke he charges through and then taunts at 275 range, but he has to reach you first — hold that gap and your poke wins.

edits.before: Galio has almost no lane pressure — his only tool against your poke is Wind Wall, which blocks a single projectile but leaves him with nothing to punish you with afterward. Bait the wall out with a low-value cast, then land your real combo. He'll likely give up on winning the lane outright and instead look to shove and roam, so ward for his ultimate coming from off-screen once he hits 6.
edits.after: Galio has almost no lane pressure — his answer to your poke is Shield of Durand, which shrugs off damage while he charges it and then taunts anything within 275 range, so never be that close when it releases. Winds of War is 11 seconds at rank 1: walk out of the tornado and poke the gap. He would rather shove and roam, so ward for Hero's Entrance arriving off-screen once he hits 6.

edits.before: Bait Wind Wall with a throwaway skill before committing your real combo
edits.after: Stay outside 275 range so Shield of Durand releases its taunt on nothing

edits.before: Use Wind Wall to block a key Cassiopeia poke or Petrifying Gaze
edits.after: Charge Shield of Durand through your poke and taunt you in close

notes: Biggest find in this matchup: five content fields credited Galio with Wind Wall, an ability he does not own — the whole 'bait the wall, then combo' plan was coaching a Yasuo mechanic. Replaced with Shield of Durand's real behaviour (charged damage reduction, then a 275-range taunt on release, 18s at rank 1). Chart: packet.defects notes the chart gives Cassiopeia 6/7 stages against a 47.24% win rate. I did not move any row on that basis — the lane really is one-sided and the deficit reads as map play through Hero's Entrance (4000-5500 range) rather than lane losses — but flagging it: if the user wants the chart to track the win rate rather than the lane, rows 5 and 6 are the ones to reconsider, and that decision needs a call from him. packet.suspectNames 'Your Petrifying Gaze' is a false positive.
